questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was not too far away from home, and that it was a good University in a nice city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall the information during the whole process has been quite difficult to get in my opinion

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only the opportunity to mail a contact person, but with quite slow response because they were very busy during the start of the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different options - some with meals included (mine wasn't). To students from EU there aren't many options since we are not guaranteed a place to stay through the university, so you just have to take what you are being offered.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a shared kitchen with 4 other students, no food included.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive and very hard to get if you are from EU. I kept calling the university everyday to hear if there were any news on my chances to get a room. I ended up getting af room 3 days before moving to Edinburgh (I know 5 other people who also kept calling and ended up getting a room, so apparently it helps).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing in itself was great, it was just really expensive and difficult to get!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you have to do all the paperwork with Learning Agreement and so on (which was a bit difficult at the University of Edinburgh, because they don't have the online system, so you have to do everything manually). When arriving in Edinburgh you have to book an appointment to show that you have arrived - this part is very easy and fast. Furthermore, you have to register for your classes. You can change between classes for the first two weeks and have the opportunities to try different classes and change classes. Though I would not recommend doing that because a lot of the classes gets filled up quite fast.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We got a contact person that we could send emails when having any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For me I had a lot of troubles registering to classes because most of the classes I wanted was already full.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for the courses you want as quick as possible, and have patience because the respondence time is quite slow since they have a lot of students to answer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my courses were 3 year BA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much the same, but a bit more interaction between students and teacher in our tutorial classes (probably because we were only around 8-10 people in each tutorial class).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Anthropology of Energy in the Global South
The Anthropology of Health and Healing
Scandinavian Civilisation A: Vikings, Sagas and the Road to Enlightenment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Anthropology of Health and Healing : because we read a lot of great texts. Also the lessons with Alexander Edmonds were very good.
Scandinavian Civilisation A: Vikings, Sagas and the Road to Enlightenment : a very interesting course seeing Scandinavia from another perspective. The teacher expects quite a lot from you which is both motivating but sometimes a bit stressfull if you have a busy week.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Only that the rent was much higher than I expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is a bit cheaper than in Denmark - especially when eating out.
The money I spend on food also reflects that I ate out a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of different societies - A LOT of different opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was in the Scandinavian Society which was nice! And also the Hill Walking club is a great way of getting on trips to the Scottish highlands.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips! Scotland really has a lot of beautiful nature. If you have the possibility I would recommend to rent a car and go by you self  or with the Hill Walking club instead of going with the ESN trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - very similar to Denmark in my opinion.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People living at my accommodation place were very young and shy(?) so not much interaction from them. I felt a bit old, but it wasn't a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness from everyone on the street etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you want accommodation through the University keep calling them eventhough it feels very uncomfortable to be that pushy.
2. Do not stress too much about keeping up with school work and remember to just enjoy the whole experience.
3. Find a hobby, society or club

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live away from home without a network and being more on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say the same as written above: establishing a network a place that is completely new to you.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
